findings.detail: Source's optional garnish '1 lemon cut into wedges (optional)' is deliberately dropped from the build, disclosed in writer_notes (no food-DB row / no ingredients.json map for the item). Optional garnish; dish as cooked is unchanged. Olive oil for avocado oil is source-sanctioned ('or fat of choice') and disclosed.

All nine spec lines sit on one consistent 4->14 (3.5x) ratio: chicken 1.5 lb -> 2381 g (1.5*453.592*3.5=2381), coconut milk 1 cup -> 3.5 cups / 840 g, tandoori 2 tbsp -> 7 tbsp / 56 g, salt 1 tbsp DC -> 3.5 tbsp / 32 g, lemon juice 3.5 tbsp / 53 g, olive oil 3.5 tbsp / 47 g, cilantro 1/4 cup -> 7/8 cup / 14 g, cauliflower 1 head -> 3.5 heads at 540 g/head, red onion 1 -> 3.5 at 70 g/small. No line departs from the recipe's ratio.

notes: Re-QA against current bytes after the renderer fix. Live page fetched successfully and matches the extraction exactly (ingredients, 4 servings, method, 590 cal source nutrition). Renderer fix confirmed in current bytes: cauliflower cost line reads 'Buy 4 heads: $7.92', no '4 1 heads' artifact. Prose cost literals match the spec's own cost fields: batch $30.70 -> $2.19/serving (30.70/14=2.193), true $37.62 -> $2.69 (37.62/14=2.687), pantry add $10.05 -> first run $47.67 (37.62+10.05). cost_ps appears only as a token, correct by construction. Tandoori Masala resolving through the adjudicated alias to bid garam-masala is an identity/pricing question the batch auditor owns; the ingredient itself (7 tbsp tandoori spice mix, 56 g) is a faithful 3.5x of the source line. At-floor 401 cal/serving rests on faithful transcription, which holds: no amount in the spec deviates from the source at 3.5x, so the one-calorie margin is not an artifact of a transcription error. Method survives intact including the split-marinade technique (vegetables in half, chicken in the remainder) and the halfway flip/rotate; the added weigh-and-portion steps are catalog boilerplate, not a technique change.
